A.name: Specific, precise proposed regulatory fix
A.instruction: Score 0-10 how concretely the comment specifies what should change: exact replacement text, a specific numeric threshold, or a precise procedural modification, versus a general expression of support or opposition. A 10: the comment proposes exact substitute wording, a specific number, or an unambiguous procedural change the agency could adopt directly. A 0: the comment states only a general 'for' or 'against' position with no specific alternative.

A.name: Traceable causal chain from the rule to the claimed effect
A.instruction: Score whether consequences are connected to the rule by a mechanism a reader can follow and check. 10 = intermediate steps are named, so the claim is falsifiable (the rule permits A, which changes B, which produces C, which matters because D). 5 = one link is stated and the rest assumed. 0 = consequences are asserted as bare outcomes with no pathway ('this will destroy the program', 'this will endanger everyone'). Judge the presence and checkability of the chain, not whether you agree with its conclusion.

A.name: Viable alternative design
A.instruction: Score 10 when the comment offers a practicable alternative regulatory design that advances the stated objective while addressing the identified defect; score 0 when it offers no alternative beyond withdrawing or enforcing the proposal.

A.name: Traceable Evidence Use
A.instruction: Score 10 when claims are supported by identifiable studies, datasets, statutes, official analyses, or clearly described observations whose relevance and limitations are explained; score 0 when claims are unsupported or rely on vague references.

A.name: Acknowledgment of tradeoffs and counterarguments
A.instruction: Score 0-10 whether the comment engages with costs, competing interests, or plausible reasons the agency might favor the opposite position, versus being purely one-sided. A 10: the comment explicitly identifies and weighs a genuine tradeoff or counter-consideration even while disagreeing. A 0: the comment shows no awareness that any opposing consideration exists.

A.name: Names a specific omission in the agency's supporting analysis
A.instruction: Score whether the comment engages the agency's own record rather than only its own position. 10 = it points to a particular thing the notice, preamble, or impact analysis failed to address - an unexamined failure mode, an uncosted burden, a population or entity class not analyzed, a required analysis not performed, a study that does not exist - and says why that omission bears on the decision. 5 = it gestures at inadequate analysis without locating the gap. 0 = the agency's record never enters; the comment argues only for its preferred outcome.

A.name: Operational Feasibility
A.instruction: Score 10 when the comment explains how affected parties would actually implement, administer, document, or comply with the proposed approach and identifies concrete operational obstacles; score 0 when implementation is discussed only abstractly.

A.name: Unintended-consequence safeguards
A.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies a plausible secondary failure or harm and proposes a concrete safeguard, monitoring step, exception, or contingency; score 0 when it predicts harm without explaining the pathway or mitigation.

A.name: Field observation that disconfirms a factual premise of the rule
A.instruction: Score whether firsthand experience is aimed at a premise rather than at a preference. 10 = the commenter reports something they have directly observed, operated, or measured that contradicts a specific factual assumption the agency is relying on (a stock estimate, an occupancy map, an achievability assumption, an exposure estimate), and identifies which assumption it contradicts. 5 = genuinely relevant firsthand experience offered as grounds for a preference, without confronting any stated premise. 0 = no firsthand observation, or observation with no bearing on any premise.

A.name: Challenge to agency assumptions
A.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies a specific premise, dataset, model, or inference in the proposal and presents concrete evidence or reasoning that could disprove or materially revise it; score 0 when it merely disagrees with the conclusion.

A.name: Identifies a conflict with operative statutory text
A.instruction: Score legal grounding by whether a conflict is demonstrated. 10 = the comment quotes or precisely cites the controlling provision and shows the proposal cannot be squared with it, or that it triggers a procedure the statute requires and the notice omitted. 5 = a relevant statute or standard is cited but the tension is asserted rather than shown. 0 = no legal grounding, or citations used as decoration. Score the demonstrated conflict, not the number or formatting of citations.

A.name: Tests whether the chosen instrument will actually bind
A.instruction: Score whether the comment interrogates the mechanism, not just the policy direction. 10 = it asks or shows whether the instrument will change behavior at all - whether a numeric limit sits above observed practice, whether a threshold will ever be triggered, whether the voluntary approach has already been tried and failed, whether the model or measurement underneath the standard can resolve the effect being regulated - and supports the answer. 5 = it questions stringency without examining whether the instrument operates. 0 = it argues only that the policy should be stronger or weaker.

A.name: Reasoning-based persuasion vs rhetorical amplification
A.instruction: Score 0-10 whether the comment's persuasive force comes from developed reasoning and evidence, versus relying on repetition, capitalization, insults, or hyperbole in place of an argument. A 10: persuasive force rests entirely on developed reasoning/evidence delivered in a measured tone, even when the position is strongly held. A 0: the comment relies on capitalized/repeated demands, insults, or hyperbolic rhetoric as a substitute for developing any argument.

A.name: Ties a requested change to a specific paragraph of regulatory text
A.instruction: Score 10 when the comment states what it wants changed AND anchors that request to an identified paragraph, section or table of the proposed text. Score 0 when no change is requested or the request floats free of any provision. Judge the anchoring of the request.

A.name: Distinguishes what the rule requires from what it merely permits
A.instruction: Score 10 when the comment correctly separates mandatory from discretionary elements of the proposal and reasons about the difference. Score 0 when it treats the proposal undifferentiated. Judge whether the distinction is drawn and used.

B.name: Organizational scale self-credentialing
B.instruction: Score 10 when the comment foregrounds quantified membership, customers, assets, market share, national reach, or institutional prestige; score 0 when it makes no organizational-scale claims.
B.upstream_parent: submitter resources, status, and perceived agency importance

B.name: Docket-lineage familiarity
B.instruction: Score 10 when the comment narrates prior filings, earlier amendments, pilot participation, waivers, agency precedents, or repeated involvement in the same regulatory process; score 0 when it treats the docket as entirely new.
B.upstream_parent: Existing agency relationship and incumbent participation in the docket

B.name: Litigation-brief posture
B.instruction: Score 10 when the comment adopts an adversarial legal-brief structure with claims of statutory conflict, plain-text mandates, legal jeopardy, formal violations, and requested legal remedies; score 0 when it lacks that posture.

B.name: Unsolicited commendation of agency staff and process
B.instruction: Score 0-10 on how much the comment praises the agency itself - its staff, its effort, its priorities, or the rulemaking process - beyond the pro-forma 'we appreciate the opportunity to comment' line, which does not count. Score 10 for explicit commendation of the work or the workers ('kudos to the staff who undertook such a massive job', 'Service staff are to be commended', 'thanks to the Department for balancing the mandate with industry concerns', 'thank you for your dedication and drive', 'Great initiative'). Score 5 for a single warm sentence about the proposal being a step in the right direction. Score 0 for no praise of the agency anywhere. Do not count praise of the underlying policy goal by third parties, and do not count the ritual opening thanks.
B.upstream_parent: coaching from an advocacy group or a naive model of how the process works - the submitter believes goodwill is currency here, which tracks submitter type rather than argument strength

B.name: Submission-production residue
B.instruction: Score 10 when visible text contains OCR corruption, duplicated headers, raw email routing, attachment placeholders, odd spacing, extraction errors, or other ingest artifacts; score 0 when the prose is cleanly presented.

B.name: Operational implementation microdetail
B.instruction: Score 10 when the comment supplies granular workflow, equipment, filing, validation, staffing, transition, or compliance-process details from inside an affected operation; score 0 when it offers only broad policy preferences or values.
B.upstream_parent: submitter proximity to regulated operations and implementation resources

B.name: Emotional-hook opening sentence before substantive content
B.instruction: Score whether the comment opens with a short, punchy, emotionally-loaded sentence or fragment functioning as a headline/attention-grabber (a declarative claim of personal harm, moral outrage, or a rhetorical jab) before any substantive policy content appears. 10 = a clear stand-alone emotional hook line opens the comment, disconnected from any immediately following factual support. 0 = the comment opens directly with a substantive claim, fact, or procedural statement, with no rhetorical hook.

B.name: Formal institutional filing apparatus / letterhead conventions
B.instruction: Score the density of formal legal/regulatory filing conventions: an addressee block, a 'Re:' case caption with docket/RIN number, numbered footnotes describing the association's membership or assets, a formal salutation ('Dear Sir or Madam'), and a closing with a professional title. 10 = full law-firm/trade-association filing apparatus present (address block + Re: caption + footnoted membership stats + titled signature block). 0 = plain conversational text with no address block, no formal salutation, and no filing conventions.
B.upstream_parent: the comment was drafted by professional legal counsel, in-house regulatory/tax staff, or a paid lobbyist following standard formal rulemaking-filing conventions

B.name: Mentions the number of members or constituents represented
B.instruction: Score 10 when the comment states how many members, employees, customers or constituents the submitter speaks for. Score 0 when no such count appears. Score only the presence of the constituency claim, never whether it makes the argument stronger.

B.name: Repeats the same sentence or phrase multiple times
B.instruction: Score 10 when a sentence or phrase is repeated verbatim three or more times in the comment. Score 0 when there is no verbatim repetition. Score only the repetition.
